newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-Ship loading seen easing prices.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-Ship loading seen easing prices.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to slide further after taking a dip overnight as a large ship on Thursday started loading fresh supplies in a Philippine port, Manila vegetable oil traders said.
MV Luctor is now starting to load some 35,000 tonnes of coconut oil in the southern port of Iligan for the European market, traders told Reuters.

Prices fell by an average $7.5 per tonne in Rotterdam overnight on reports of the arrival of Luctor in the Philippines and minimal damage on the coconut crop by a major typhoon that swamped Luzon island, a senior trader said.
Coconut oil was last traded at $640 per tonne CIF for May/June shipment on Wednesday, the trader added.
Talk of a possible delay of a major shipment of Philippine coconut oil in June or July pushed prices of the commodity by $20 per tonne since May 19.
Luctor replaced MV Blue Sapphire which was scheduled to load 35,000 tonnes of Philippine coconut oil. Sapphire was stuck in China, traders said.
"With technical problems on the vessel solved, expect the market to go back to fundamentals," said one trader.
Luctor is expected to leave Iligan port on June 5 and scheduled to arrive in Rotterdam after one month.
Traders said they see the market giving back the $20 it gained in the past several days with improving supplies from the Philippines.
The Oil World newsletter forecast Philippine coconut oil exports in the 1997 calendar year at 830,000 tonnes, up 200,000 from 1996, citing a sharp increase in export availability from June onwards.
Manila traders said a number of buyers bought a lot of coconut oil in the past several days, including at least 7,000 tonnes clinched by a U.S. buyer Wednesday.
